note: Frameworks and standards for AI governance, threat modelling and security controls. Versions checked against each owner's page or a reliable report of it. Reference only, not an assessment.

groups.name: Governance and risk
groups.about: How organisations govern AI and manage its risks.

groups.name: Threat modelling and secure AI development
groups.about: How AI systems are attacked, and how to build and run them securely.

groups.name: Implementation controls
groups.about: General cyber security controls and assurance frameworks that AI systems sit within.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 42001
standards.what: Certifiable management system standard for AI: policies, roles, risk and impact assessment across the AI lifecycle
standards.status: No amendments. Companion standards cover impact assessment (ISO/IEC 42005, May 2025) and certification bodies (ISO/IEC 42006, July 2025). UKAS accredited BSI as the first UK certification body in January 2026

changes.text: UKAS grants BSI the first UK accreditation to certify AI management systems to ISO/IEC 42001

standards.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
standards.what: Voluntary framework to govern, map, measure and manage AI risks, with profiles for specific uses
standards.version: AI RMF 1.0, plus the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1, July 2024)
standards.status: Being revised under the US AI Action Plan; no revised version yet. Concept note for a critical infrastructure profile published April 2026

changes.text: Concept note for an AI RMF profile on trustworthy AI in critical infrastructure

standards.name: MITRE ATLAS
standards.what: Knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems, modelled on ATT&CK, with real-world case studies
standards.status: May 2026 update added 45+ techniques and sub-techniques, 10+ mitigations and 20+ case studies, with more on agentic AI. Now released monthly

changes.text: Secure AI v2 update: 45+ new techniques, 10+ mitigations, 20+ case studies; move to monthly releases
First 2026 update adds AI agent techniques, including tool credential harvesting and tool data poisoning

standards.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
standards.what: The ten most critical security risks for applications built on large language models
standards.status: Released with a new Agent Control Standard. Sits alongside the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications

changes.text: 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications released, with the Agent Control Standard

standards.name: Guidelines for secure AI system development
standards.owner: NCSC and CISA, with international partners
standards.what: Guidance on secure design, development, deployment, and operation and maintenance of AI systems
standards.status: No update since 2023. Built on by the DSIT AI Cyber Security Code of Practice and ETSI EN 304 223

standards.name: AI Cyber Security Code of Practice
standards.what: Voluntary UK baseline of security principles for developers and operators of AI systems, with an implementation guide
standards.status: Basis for the European standard ETSI EN 304 223 (December 2025). The Code is due to be updated to align with it

changes.text: ETSI EN 304 223, built on the Code, published as a European standard; the Code will be updated to match

standards.name: ISO/IEC 27001
standards.what: Certifiable information security management system standard, with Annex A controls
standards.status: No AI-specific requirements. Often used alongside ISO/IEC 42001

standards.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
standards.what: Outcomes to govern, identify, protect, detect, respond and recover, used to set and assess cyber security targets
standards.status: Cyber AI Profile (NIST IR 8596) in preliminary draft since December 2025; comments closed January 2026, next draft awaited

changes.text: Preliminary draft Cyber AI Profile (NIST IR 8596) published for comment

standards.name: Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)
standards.what: Outcome-based framework for assessing the cyber resilience of essential services, used by UK regulators and the NHS
standards.status: Version 4.0 added outcomes on AI-related risks. Further versions expected to follow the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill

changes.text: CAF 4.0 published, including AI-related cyber risks

standards.name: Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT)
standards.what: Annual self-assessment for organisations with access to NHS patient data and systems; CAF-aligned for larger NHS organisations
standards.status: 2026-27 standard published with updated CAF-aligned audit guidance
